BiblicalUsage: lishshân means speech, a language, and it does large work in the story. In Daniel 3:4, "and languages"; and in Daniel 3:29, "and language". In Daniel 4:1, "and languages"; and in Daniel 6:25, "and languages".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the languages of Babylon are God's audience — every people, nation, and language heard the king's decree, and then heard Daniel's God praised. I hold that no tongue is outside His reach: Nebuchadnezzar wrote to all languages, and Darius did the same. My position is that my language is one of many, and God speaks them all.
